wave.summary: Replaced the BrainScoutView stub with the full implementation. A form-wrapped input (placeholder 'Type a seed idea…') plus a 'Scout it 🔭' submit button (disabled while the trimmed phrase is empty; Enter key submits via native form submit) calls expand(phrase, seed) with seed = Math.floor(Math.random()*2**31) rolled at the UI boundary. Renders result.rungs as .ladder-rung cards in LADDER_RUNGS order (Weekend/Week/Month/Moonshot) and result.remixes as .remix-card cards, each with a .tag-chip label (rung name or lens) and the expanded text. A Re-scout button re-rolls the seed via expand(result.seedPhrase, newSeed), keeping the same phrase. Each card gets its own Copy (navigator.clipboard?.writeText guarded, flips to 'Copied!') and Save (addFavorite({kind:'scout', label, text, id: item.id}), flips to 'Saved ✓' whether newly added or already present) button, following PromptCard's pattern and using the plain favorites functions (addFavorite/favId/loadFavorites) rather than the known-buggy useFavorites hook. Only reused existing frozen classes (.scout-view, .scout-input-row, .scout-note, .ladder-rung, .remix-card, .tag-chip) with minor inline styles for the new card body/actions layout — app.css and no other file was touched. No test-file location was in my file scope (src/ui/BrainScoutView.tsx only), so no BrainScoutView-specific test was added; I verified via `npx tsc -b` (clean) and the full `npx vitest run` suite (110/110 passing, including App.test.tsx's Brain Scout tab/section assertions, which still pass unchanged).

wave.summary: Implemented share-link URL bootstrap wiring entirely within App.tsx/App.test.tsx, per scope. In App.tsx, the seed and filters useState hooks now use lazy initializers that call decodeShare(window.location.search) once on mount; a valid decode sets the exact shared {seed, filters} so the memoized generate() call renders the string-identical prompt, while an invalid/absent query falls through to the pre-existing empty state (seed: null, filters: {}). Added a "Copy share link" button, rendered only in the generator view below PromptCard when a prompt exists, that builds `${location.origin}${location.pathname}?${encodeShare({seed, filters})}` and writes it via navigator.clipboard?.writeText (guarded with try/catch), flipping its label to "Link copied!" on click; it resets on a fresh Spark tap. Did not touch PromptCard.tsx or any component outside the two in-scope files. In App.test.tsx, added two tests: (a) using history.replaceState to stub location.search to '?seed=123&subject=law' before an isolated remount, then asserting the rendered .prompt-card's .prompt-text equals generate(123,{subject:'law'}).text; (b) clicking the new .share-link-button with a mocked clipboard and asserting writeText received a string containing 'seed=' and the label flipped to 'Link copied!'. All prior tests (rendered against the default empty-search app from the outer beforeEach) still pass unmodified, confirming the mount-bootstrap doesn't disturb the normal empty-state path. Ran the full suite (112 tests, 6 files) and `tsc -b` — both clean. Note: the worktree ships without node_modules (git worktrees don't carry gitignored dirs); I symlinked node_modules to the target repo's pre-installed copy to run tests — no packages were installed, vendored, or manifests touched, and the symlink itself is gitignored and was not committed. Two tracked build-cache files (.tsbuild/tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo) picked up incidental timestamp diffs from running tsc/vitest; left unstaged/uncommitted since they're outside file scope.

wave.summary: Fixed KI-1: useFavorites() was calling useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, loadFavorites, loadFavorites) directly, but loadFavorites() returns a fresh array reference every call — violating getSnapshot's "same reference until data changes" contract and causing React to throw "Maximum update depth exceeded" on mount. In src/state/favorites.ts, added an internal module-level `cachedSnapshot: Favorite[] | null`, a private `getSnapshot()` that lazily populates it on first read and reuses the cached reference thereafter, and invalidation (`cachedSnapshot = null`) inside `notify()` so any real write (add/remove) recomputes it on the next read. `useFavorites()` now wires `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getSnapshot)` instead of loadFavorites. Public API is unchanged: loadFavorites still returns a fresh array on every call (existing consumers/tests unaffected), addFavorite/removeFavorite/favId/subscribe/useFavorites signatures untouched. Did not touch src/ui/FavoritesView.tsx per instructions. All 15 pre-existing tests in favorites.test.ts pass byte-for-byte unchanged. Appended two new tests: (1) mounts a real React component via react-dom/client createRoot + act, asserting mount succeeds, textContent reflects the store, and the component re-renders exactly once per store change (addFavorite twice inside act, checking both textContent and a render counter) — I verified this test genuinely fails with the reported "Maximum update depth exceeded" error when I temporarily reverted useFavorites to the broken loadFavorites-as-getSnapshot wiring, then restored the fix; (2) getSnapshot referential stability — renders a capture component twice via a prop change with no store write between them and asserts Object.is equality of the captured array, then writes and asserts a new, distinct, correctly-updated reference is produced. Also added a `globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true` line in the test file (in scope) to silence a spurious React act() environment warning; this doesn't touch app code. Full `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. Note: the worktree ships without node_modules (git worktree doesn't include it), so I symlinked node_modules from the target repo into the worktree purely to run tests locally — this is untracked/gitignored and was never staged or committed.

wave.summary: Fixed the run-on-sentence bug at generate()'s single assembly point in src/core/generate.ts. Added a pure helper withTerminalPunctuation(text) that trims trailing whitespace and appends '.' only if the text doesn't already end in . ! or ?. Applied it to both the resolved template body and the twist before joining them as `${body} Twist: ${twistText}`. No template data files were touched, and no additional rand() call is consumed, so the existing determinism/string-equality tests (which rely on identical two-call output) still pass unchanged. Extended src/core/generate.test.ts with a T-020 describe block: one test iterates getTemplates({}) grouped into its 12 subject x difficulty buckets, sweeps 200 seeds per bucket to positively confirm every one of the 48 templates is exercised (not just probabilistically likely to be), and asserts every produced text matches /[.!?] Twist: / and ends in [.!?]; a second test sweeps 200 unfiltered seeds for the same shape. Verified TDD red state first (2 new tests failed pre-fix showing exactly the run-on bug, e.g. '...hardcode Twist: Add a simple...'), then green after the fix, with all 21 pre-existing tests in the file passing throughout. Provisioned the worktree per Step 0, verified git-common-dir and .swarm/SPEC.md, and symlinked node_modules from the target repo into the worktree (untracked, covered by .gitignore's node_modules/ pattern) purely to run vitest/tsc locally — nothing outside the file scope was modified or committed.
